gentle ground on the source itself, where the soil is made from the rock. The stone weathers out and stays on top while the soft rock washes away: walk slowly over the loose stones on the surface, the bare patches and the washes. A big area: start at the road point and work outward.
broken, angular pieces (within about 3 km of the source; Attal & Lave 2009)
Best during or right after rain (Landon 2019) and before the plants come up (RI16 p.15: stones can be "hidden by barren deposits or vegetation").
High potential for obsidian covers 0.2% of the land. In the test on 14 record finds the model was never built on, 7 (50%) lay on or near it (63.4 times the random-ground baseline)

light and brittle. Carried as float into the basins around its domes ("in the basins to the north and south of Glass Buttes", Stueber & Skinner 2015 p.195), in alluvium below Idaho's Silver City Range (Pink 2023 p.19), as "water-worn obsidian pebbles" on Yakima River bars (RI16 p.32). No source gives a distance; WHAT uses the volcanic wear class (CONV). Fresh surfaces hydrate (Friedman & Smith 1960).
